cues.text: Hello. Do you mind if I ask you some questions about your journey today? We’re doing a customer satisfaction survey.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Yes. OK. I’ve got about ten minutes before my train home leaves. I’m on a day trip.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: Great. Thank you. So first of all, could you tell me your name?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: It’s Sophie Bird.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: Thank you. And would you mind telling me what you do?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: I’m a journalist.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: Oh really? That must be interesting.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Yes. It is.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: So was the reason for your visit here today work?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Actually, it’s my day off. I came here to do some shopping.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: On right.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: But I do sometimes come here for work.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: OK. Now I’d like to ask some questions about your journey today, if that’s OK.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Yes. No problem.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: Right, so can you tell me which station you’re travelling back to?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Staunfirth, where I live.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: Can I just check the spelling? S-T-A-U-N-F-I-R-T-H?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: That’s right.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: And you travelled from there this morning?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Yes.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: OK, good. Next, can I ask what kind of ticket you bought? I assume it wasn’t a season ticket, as you don’t travel every day.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: That’s right. No, I just got a normal return ticket. I don’t have a rail card so I didn’t get any discount. I keep meaning to get one because it’s a lot cheaper.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: Yes – you’d have saved 20% on your ticket today. So you paid the full price for your ticket?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: I paid £23.70.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: OK. Do you think that’s good value for money?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Not really. I think it’s too much for a journey that only takes 45 minutes.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: Yes, that’s one of the main complaints we get. So, you didn’t buy your ticket in advance?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: No. I know it’s cheaper if you buy a week in advance but I didn’t know I was coming then.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: I know. You can’t always plan ahead. So, did you buy it this morning?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: No, it was yesterday.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: Right. And do you usually buy your tickets at the station?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Well, I do usually but the ticket office closes early and I hate using ticket machines. I think ticket offices should be open for longer hours. There’s always a queue for the machines and they’re often out of order.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: A lot of customers are saying the same thing.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: So to answer your question … I got an e-ticket online.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: OK. Thank you. Now I’d like to ask you about your satisfaction with your journey. So what would you say you were most satisfied with today?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Well, I like the wifi on the train. It’s improved a lot. It makes it easier for me to work if I want to.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: That’s the first time today anyone’s mentioned that. It’s good to get some positive feedback on that.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Mmm.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: And, is there anything you weren’t satisfied with?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Well, normally, the trains run on time and are pretty reliable but today there was a delay; the train was about 15 minutes behind schedule.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: OK. I’ll put that down. Now I’d also like to ask about the facilities at this station. You’ve probably noticed that the whole station’s been upgraded. What are you most satisfied with?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: I think the best thing is that they’ve improved the amount of information about train times etc. that’s given to passengers – it’s much clearer – before there was only one board and I couldn’t always see it properly – which was frustrating.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: That’s good. And is there anything you’re not satisfied with?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Let’s see … I think things have generally improved a lot. The trains are much more modern and I like the new café. But one thing is that there aren’t enough places to sit down, especially on the platforms.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: OK – so I’ll put ‘seating’ down, shall I, as the thing you’re least satisfied with?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Yes, OK.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: Can I ask your opinion about some of the other facilities? We’d like feedback on whether people are satisfied, dissatisfied or neither satisfied nor dissatisfied.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: OK.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: What about the parking at the station?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Well to be honest, I don’t really have an opinion as I never use it.
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: So, neither satisfied nor dissatisfied for that then.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Yes, I suppose so …
cues.speaker: SOPHIE

cues.text: OK, and what about …?
cues.speaker: MAN
